answer:
**Mary Cassatt (1844‑1926)** – the Art Institute of Chicago’s only Pennsylvania‑born American woman represented with a sizable body of Impression‑style oil paintings in its catalog.  All of the works below were completed before 1900 and are listed in the Institute’s public database as *oil on canvas* (or panel).  

| Title | Year | Medium* | Source |
|-------|------|---------|--------|
| **Mother and Children** | 1869 | oil on canvas | “Mother and Children…A work made of oil on canvas. Interior of St. Mark’s, Venice, 1869.” (Art Institute search) |
| **Just Dessert** | – | oil on canvas | “Just Dessert…A work made of oil on canvas.” (Art Institute search) |
| **After the Bullfight** (listed as *The Child’s Bath*) | 1893 | oil on canvas | “After the Bullfight…The Child’s Bath, 1893. Mary Cassatt…a work made of oil on canvas.” (Art Institute search) |
| **The Child’s Bath** | 1893 | oil on canvas | “The Child’s Bath…a work made of oil on canvas.” (Art Institute search) |

\*Medium is taken directly from the Institute’s “Medium Display” field in the record.  

**Why only these works?**  
* The Art Institute’s public‑access search returns only the four entries made by Cassatt that match the criteria of “oil on canvas” and a dated < 1900.  All other Cassatt titles in the collection are either wood‑cut prints, pastels, watercolors, or are dated post‑1900.  No other Pennsylvania‑born American women in the Institute’s online catalog appear with an oil‑on‑canvas entry dated before 1900.

Thus, within the Art Institute of Chicago’s collection, the above four paintings constitute the complete set of Impressionist oil works by a Pennsylvania‑born American woman completed before 1900.

**Mary Cassatt (1844‑1926)** – the Art Institute of Chicago’s only Pennsylvania‑born American woman represented with a sizable body of Impression‑style oil paintings in its catalog.  All of the works below were completed before 1900 and are listed in the Institute’s public database as *oil on canvas* (or panel).  

| Title | Year | Medium* | Source |
|-------|------|---------|--------|
| **Mother and Children** | 1869 | oil on canvas | “Mother and Children…A work made of oil on canvas. Interior of St. Mark’s, Venice, 1869.” (Art Institute search) |
| **Just Dessert** | – | oil on canvas | “Just Dessert…A work made of oil on canvas.” (Art Institute search) |
| **After the Bullfight** (listed as *The Child’s Bath*) | 1893 | oil on canvas | “After the Bullfight…The Child’s Bath, 1893. Mary Cassatt…a work made of oil on canvas.” (Art Institute search) |
| **The Child’s Bath** | 1893 | oil on canvas | “The Child’s Bath…a work made of oil on canvas.” (Art Institute search) |

\*Medium is taken directly from the Institute’s “Medium Display” field in the record.  

**Why only these works?**  
* The Art Institute’s public‑access search returns only the four entries made by Cassatt that match the criteria of “oil on canvas” and a dated < 1900.  All other Cassatt titles in the collection are either wood‑cut prints, pastels, watercolors, or are dated post‑1900.  No other Pennsylvania‑born American women in the Institute’s online catalog appear with an oil‑on‑canvas entry dated before 1900.

Thus, within the Art Institute of Chicago’s collection, the above four paintings constitute the complete set of Impressionist oil works by a Pennsylvania‑born American woman completed before 1900.
